# Test evidence — 2026-10-22

Everything below was executed in this session unless it is explicitly marked
**not run**. Evidence files are generated by the runner, not hand-written.

## 1. Environment (actual)

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Host | Linux sandbox, no PHP binary, no MySQL, no WordPress |
| PHP used | **8.4.1 compiled to WebAssembly** (`php-wasm` 0.2.0 via Node 22.22.3) |
| Extensions present | hash, tokenizer, filter, pdo, ctype, json, pcre |
| Extensions absent | sodium, openssl, mbstring, dom, dns |
| WordPress | not installed; `tests/bootstrap.php` supplies minimal API stubs backed by in-memory state |
| Repository state | branch `arena/a0b93feb-ajith-security-suite-pro`, base commit `4728e6c` |

Consequence: everything requiring sodium/openssl/DOM/DNS/mysqli or a real
WordPress request is **not run**, and the corresponding assertions are recorded
as `SKIP`, never as pass. WebAssembly also inflates CPU timings relative to a
normal PHP-FPM process.

## 2. Commands

```bash
# syntax lint of every PHP file (token_get_all with TOKEN_PARSE)
node tests/tools/php-wasm-runner.mjs            # runs lint + suite

# equivalent with a local PHP binary
php tests/lint.php .
php tests/run-tests.php --verbose --json=docs/evidence/phpunit-results.json
```

Generated evidence:

* `docs/evidence/lint.json` — files linted, failures
* `docs/evidence/phpunit-results.json` — per-assertion results, PHP version, extension probe
* `docs/evidence/phpunit-results.json` timing detail for the `performance` group

## 4. Defects found and fixed by this suite

| # | Defect (proof) | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | A parameter named `password`, `pwd`, `log`, `token`, `session` or `code` was **never inspected**: `evidence()` dropped credential subtrees entirely, so `?password=' OR 1=1-- -` passed the WAF. Test `waf-credential-keys` failed 7/7 before the fix. | Credential values are collected separately (`credential_values`) and screened with injection-only rules; values are never logged. |
| 2 | Single-segment traversal `../wp-config.php` (and `%2e%2e%2f…`) was missed: the rule required two `../` segments. Test failed 2/5. | `GWQSH_Firewall::traversal()` correlates one parent segment. |
| 3 | Quoted SQL tautology `1' OR '1'='1` and the whole tautology family were missed (only numeric `1' OR 1=1--` matched). | Tautology families added to `sql_high_confidence()`. |
| 4 | Comment-obfuscated keywords (`1 UNION/**/SELECT …`, `/*!50000UNION*/`) were missed. | Comment-tolerant union/select and version-comment correlation. |
| 5 | Serialized object nested in an array (`a:1:{i:0;O:7:"WP_User":…}`) was missed; only objects starting the value matched. | `serialized_object()` matches the object shape anywhere in a value. |
| 6 | Executable PHP in request data (`<?php system($_GET[c]); ?>`) had no rule at all. | New **report-first** rule `GWQSH-1017` (needs `enforce_new` to block). |
| 7 | `advanced()` walked the evidence tree twice per call (once for values, once for SQL), on every request. | Single bounded walk per collection. |

## 5. Deliberately aggressive detections (documented, not hidden)

`tests/cases/090-false-positives.php` asserts that these benign-looking inputs
**are** flagged, so operators see the trade-off:

* prose containing `sleep(8)`-style calls,
* prose containing `and 'alpha' = 'beta'`,
* prose containing `or 1 = 1`,
* a `<?php` snippet pasted into a support form (report-only rule),
* prose containing `;cat /etc/hosts`.

Mitigations available to a site owner: WAF report-only mode, exact PATH
exclusions, IP allowlist, per-rule approval gates.

## 6. Not run (do not treat as passing)

* WordPress activation/deactivation, Free→Pro migration, settings persistence.
* WooCommerce checkout, Gutenberg publish, REST/AJAX round trips, multisite.
* Browser passkey registration/login; TOTP UI flow.
* Malware scan against a representative corpus; quarantine/restore round trip.
* Backup creation, staged import, cutover, rollback.
* Alert delivery (email/Slack), cron reliability, scheduled reports.
* PHPCS, PHPStan, Plugin Check, `composer audit`, secret scanning (no toolchain
  and no Composer manifest in the repository root).
* Production latency (p50/p95), memory ceilings and concurrency.
